title: ANDS Studio overall product concept
walkthrough:
You land on a page with a top bar branded "ANDS Studio · guided ANDS filing" and chips for "Help", "My dossiers", "Portfolio", "Registry" and "Correspondence". Before the hero, a one-time external-prerequisites checklist can appear; once you dismiss it, the hero shows. The headline reads "File your ANDS with Health Canada — guided end to end." The body copy states an Abbreviated New Drug Submission is one of the most complex filings a company can make, and that the tool walks you through it step by step, every term explained in plain language with the regulatory vocabulary kept precise, the right pathway chosen, and readiness visible until it's ready to send. The primary button is "Start my submission →", a secondary link reads "Or open your dossiers — every product in submission →", and a footnote says "Grounded in real Health Canada process · your progress is saved automatically". Returning later shows "Loading your filing…" and resumes your saved session.

Starting opens a three-column layout: a step rail of journey stages on the left, the active step's card in the middle, and a right-hand panel with a "submission tower" of module tiles plus a readiness card. The top bar adds a readiness chip — "Ready to file" or a percentage like "34% ready" — and a "Start over" button. The overall register is calm: one primary thing per surface, with detail tucked behind expanders.

The "Draft completeness check" card shows a pass/fail line ("● NO STRUCTURAL ISSUES" or "● N issue(s)") that is always visible. On its face it names the profile and version and qualifies it "(structural; not HC eValidator)", with a disclaimer line beneath. Buttons "What this does / does NOT check" and "Rule catalogue (CA-E/CA-W ids)" expand the coverage detail and a browsable rule catalogue; findings carry rule ids. A "Technical check & report" expander holds the PDF-header/encryption sub-check and CSV/JSON report export. Repeated copy states this is a presence/format check — not a Health Canada review and not full eCTD technical validation — and tells you to run Health Canada's eValidator before you transmit.

On "Account & security", a "Who you are here" section shows your email, workspace (from the account record, isolated to this workspace), role, and a role permission matrix. You can add a time-based one-time code (TOTP) from a standard authenticator app via "Set up authenticator app →"; the flow shows a secret, a "Copy setup link", and a 6-digit confirmation, and states nothing is enforced until the code verifies. A separate section covers a workspace-wide MFA mandate. "Password & sessions" lists plain rules (10-character minimum, forgot-password reset, 12-hour sessions) with cryptographic detail behind a "For your IT department" expander. "Deployment & data residency" states ANDS Studio is self-hosted — nothing leaves your environment except packages you transmit — that cross-workspace reads are refused at the API, and records honest limits: single sign-on (SAML/OIDC) and SCIM provisioning are not yet available, with SIEM streaming on the roadmap. A workspace Part-11 audit viewer with inspection export and a roadmap card of not-yet-built enterprise capabilities close the page.

Acronyms throughout carry plain-language tooltips. Lifecycle operators, deficiency windows, bilingual and XML Product Monograph, collaboration, and a portfolio/PM layer with owner/client/deadline columns are surfaced across the app rather than on this landing surface.
